title: Norvexa sealant labels: neutralize eight mixed-light cartridge shots to an in-frame grey card, author a graphite Pro colorway from the orange-cap hero, vectorize the wordmark + hazard pictograms, and data-merge one press-ready CMYK label per SKU/variant
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork packaging brief (a construction-chemicals maker wanting its legacy product-label PDFs rebuilt into an editable, maintainable Adobe layout system: "49 products, many with 1-3 variants", "different bottle and canister sizes", "recreate the labels based on the existing design (no new design required)", supplied "updated texts, product images, barcodes, safety data sheets, H/P statements", deliver "editable, print-ready files (CMYK, with bleed)") and laundered to a fictional maker, 'Norvexa Bauchemie GmbH' — no real company, product, or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original ask (author a layout from scratch) is NOT connector-doable — document_merge_data_layout cannot compose a layout and cannot place multiple records on one page, and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields. So the client is modeled as having already rebuilt ONE master label into a genuinely hand-authored InDesign template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> and FOUR @-prefixed image-path columns (the product photo, the SKU's hazard pictogram, the SKU's EAN barcode, and the shared brand wordmark). The Adobe chain does the real production the brief rewards: neutralize every raw line-side cartridge photo to the 18% grey card it carries so the whole batch shares one white point, decide per frame how far to move white balance without washing out a product's genuine color, author a graphite 'Pro' colorway of the orange-cap hero without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the scanned brand wordmark and the regulated GHS hazard pictograms so they stay razor-sharp on press, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export one press-ready CMYK-with-bleed PDF per SKU/variant. No new label is designed — the master layout is a supplied input, exactly as the brief says 'no new design required'.
one_line_ask: Neutralize eight mixed-lighting cartridge photos to the grey card each one carries so they read as one matched set, decide per frame how far to move white balance without killing any product's genuine color, author a graphite Pro colorway of the orange-cap hero without reshooting, prep and vectorize the scanned wordmark and the hazard pictograms, then data-merge the client's authored InDesign master against the per-SKU/variant roster to produce one press-ready CMYK-with-bleed label PDF per row.
full_brief: Norvexa Bauchemie GmbH, a European maker of construction sealants and adhesives, is moving its product-label artwork off legacy flat PDFs onto a maintainable, print-ready data-merge system. The team has already rebuilt ONE master label into a genuinely authored InDesign template — a 90 x 130 mm cartridge/canister wrap laid out with 3 mm bleed at 300 DPI CMYK, carrying live data-merge fields (<<product_name>>, <<variant>>, <<net_content>>, <<sku>>, <<batch_prefix>>, <<h_statements>>, <<p_statements>>, <<usage_de>>) plus four image frames (the product shot, the SKU's GHS hazard pictogram, the SKU's EAN barcode, and the brand wordmark in the masthead). What they need now is production, not design: bind the master to the range and output one press-ready file per SKU/variant. Here is the work. First, the photos. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you eight cartridge/canister photos shot over two shifts on the line under whatever light was there — some under cool fluorescents, some under warm window light, a couple underexposed, one blown out — so straight out of the folder they are a mismatched jumble, and a label run built from mismatched shots looks cheap on shelf. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into a corner of every frame. Bring the whole set to one consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each shot to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the batch shares one white point. Do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each frame was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target. Be careful — one of these products is a polyurethane wood adhesive that is genuinely a warm amber/tan color; if its grey card already reads neutral, do not 'cool' it chasing an imagined cast, or you will strip the color the product actually is. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set is matched, not eyeballed. Second, a variant colorway without a reshoot: our top SKU photographs with a bright safety-orange nozzle cap, and marketing wants a premium 'Pro' colorway of that same shot where the cap reads as a dark graphite/gunmetal finish instead — a deep, desaturated metallic grey, riding the real highlights and shadow of the cap so the plastic still looks like plastic. Only the cap: no flat dead-fill, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the cartridge body or the background. Third, the marks. Our brand wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp for the label masthead (it must not look like a fuzzy scan on press). And the regulated GHS hazard pictograms we hand you as small flat rasters must be crisp vectors so they stay sharp at any label size. Finally, build the labels: we have hand-built the InDesign master with the real placeholder fields and four image slots (product photo, hazard pictogram, EAN barcode, and the wordmark masthead), and we are giving you the roster; merge them so every SKU/variant gets its own single label with its German copy and H/P statements bound verbatim, its matching graded photo dropped in, the correct hazard pictogram and barcode placed, and the crisp wordmark in the masthead, then hand back a print-ready ~300 DPI CMYK-with-3mm-bleed PDF covering every row (one page per SKU/variant, the Pro colorway simply among them). Bind the German copy and the CLP H/P statements verbatim from the roster — do not paraphrase our compliance text. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set matched to one white point; the Pro cap a natural graphite under the real light; the wordmark and pictograms crisp vectors; and exactly one finished label per roster row.

inputs.name: norvexa_label_master.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD 90 x 130 mm portrait sealant-cartridge wrap label with 3 mm bleed and CMYK intent, rebuilt to match Norvexa's existing legacy label look — ONE SKU per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<variant>>, <<net_content>>, <<sku>>, <<batch_prefix>>, <<h_statements>>, <<p_statements>>, <<usage_de>>, plus FOUR @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to four separate image frames: a product-photo frame bound to @product (the matching graded cartridge photo), a hazard-pictogram frame bound to @pictogram (the row's vectorized GHS symbol), an EAN-barcode frame bound to @barcode (the row's barcode), and a masthead frame bound to @wordmark (the shared vectorized brand wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, every image reaches the label ONLY as a merge bind through one of these four frames — nothing is dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and all four image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template (literal/outlined text) would NOT bind, and a multi-up grid cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: Modeled as the client's already-rebuilt master label (the brief's 'recreate ... no new design', done once). document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields PLUS genuine @image-path columns — it cannot be connector-generated, so it is a SUPPLIED input, not a chain output. The .indd extension (never .pdf) and the explicit 'not a convert_pdf_to_indd output' note are the correction to the killed original design, which supplied a .pdf and then ran convert_pdf_to_indd before merging — a path its own notes admitted would not bind. FOUR @image columns mean the merge resolves four prepped assets per row: the row's graded product photo (@product), the row's vectorized hazard pictogram (@pictogram), the row's barcode (@barcode), and the shared vectorized wordmark (@wordmark, identical every row) — so the chain-produced marks reach the label as merge binds, never free-form placement.

inputs.name: norvexa_label_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns product_name,variant,net_content,sku,batch_prefix,h_statements,p_statements,usage_de,@product,@pictogram,@barcode,@wordmark holding NINE sealant SKU/variant rows across the MS-Polymer, Hybrid, Acryl, Butyl and PU-adhesive ranges: (1) MS-Polymer 600 ml Grau, (2) MS-Polymer 290 ml Weiss, (3) Hybrid 290 ml Grau, (4) PU-Holzkleber 310 ml (a genuinely amber/tan polyurethane wood adhesive), (5) Acryl 300 ml Weiss, (6) Acryl 300 ml Grau, (7) Butyl 290 ml Schwarz, (8) Hybrid Pro 600 ml Grau, and (9) Hybrid Pro 600 ml Grau 'Graphit-Edition' (the Pro colorway variant of row 8, same product with the graphite-cap treatment). Each row carries realistic German usage text in usage_de, real-format CLP H- and P-statement strings (e.g. 'H317 Kann allergische Hautreaktionen verursachen.' / 'P280 Schutzhandschuhe tragen.'), a batch_prefix, and a 13-digit EAN-format sku. The @product column names the matching prepped photo file (the graded cartridge photo, e.g. @prod_ms600.jpg; rows 8 and 9 reference the standard graded hero and the graphite-variant graded hero respectively). The @pictogram column names that SKU's single vectorized GHS symbol so all three vectorized pictograms get used across the range: @ghs05_corrosion.svg for the strongly-hazardous MS-Polymer 600 (row 1), @ghs02_flame.svg for the flammable Hybrid and Butyl SKUs (rows 3 and 7), and @ghs07_exclamation.svg for the irritant SKUs (rows 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9). The @barcode column names that SKU's own EAN barcode file. The @wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file — @norvexa_wordmark.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every label. Column names for the bound text fields must exactly match the InDesign merge fields, and the four @columns must match the template's four image frames.
inputs.realism_notes: One row per SKU/variant is the core of the 'many with 1-3 variants' brief; German copy + CLP H/P statements come only from the CSV so they are never paraphrased; headers match the authored .indd fields and all four @image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds. NO COLUMN TELEGRAPHS THE PHOTO TREATMENT: the @product column references the agent's own graded output names (produced only after the agent decides each frame's grade), the @pictogram value is a regulatory hazard-class fact (which GHS symbol legally applies to which product), not a hint about how to grade a photo, and nothing in the CSV states which capture is tilted, which is warm/cool, or which is the amber-product trap. @pictogram varies per row across all three vectorized symbols; @barcode varies per row (per-SKU EAN); @wordmark is identical in all nine rows. Nine rows => the merge must produce exactly nine finished labels.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera capture, ~3800-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution still straight off the camera before any crop), of a 600 ml grey MS-Polymer sealant cartridge/canister standing on a plain line-side table, with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Shot under cool bluish fluorescent light, the frame tilted about 4 degrees off level, flat dull workshop exposure, faint dust and a distracting shelf edge behind. Real plastic and metal texture, label area blank, no CGI gloss, candid documentary QA-photo feel. The grey card is clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~3800-4500 px long edge (NOT a ~1024-1536 px AI-gen raster) precisely so the crop to the label's product frame fills at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Cool cast + ~4 deg tilt: needs both an auto_straighten and a warm-direction neutralization to its in-frame grey card. Neutral filename (capture_NN scheme, shared by all eight photos, same extension) so nothing in the name reveals the cast, tilt, or which frame is the trap — the agent must open each to decide its grade.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 290 ml white MS-Polymer cartridge on a line-side bench, 18% grey card in a corner. Shot under cool fluorescent light, frame roughly level, slightly flat exposure. Real matte-plastic texture, blank label zone, candid factory look, no studio gloss. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool cast, LEVEL (no straighten needed — deciding that is part of the triage). White product: the neutralization to its grey card must not tint the white body. Neutral capture_NN filename; treatment not disclosed by name.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 290 ml grey Hybrid-sealant cartridge on a workshop table, 18% grey card in a corner. Shot under warm window light, frame tilted about 3 degrees, exposure okay. Real plastic texture, blank label surface, candid QA aesthetic, no CGI. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: WARM cast + ~3 deg tilt: this frame must be COOLED (opposite direction from the cool frames) to neutralize its grey card, AND straightened — proving the batch is not uniformly one direction. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 310 ml polyurethane wood-adhesive cartridge whose cured product and nozzle are GENUINELY a warm amber/tan color, standing on a line-side table with a photographic 18% grey card in a corner. Shot under near-neutral balanced light so the grey card already reads close to neutral; the amber warmth is the real product color, not a white-balance error. Frame roughly level, clean exposure. Real plastic and cured-adhesive texture, blank label zone, candid documentary feel. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The product is honestly amber/tan and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card is ALREADY neutral — the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction it used on the fluorescent frames, or that 'cools an imagined warm cast' because the frame looks amber, will push this card OFF neutral and strip the product's real color. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not by how the product looks or by the batch. Neutral capture_NN filename — nothing names this as the trap.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 300 ml white Acryl-sealant cartridge on a bench, 18% grey card in a corner. Shot flat and clearly UNDEREXPOSED, near-neutral cast. Real matte-plastic texture, blank label zone, candid factory documentation, no gloss. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: The dominant problem here is TONAL, not white balance: exposure must be lifted (and contrast/clarity added) before the grey card can be read, then neutralized to the shared white point — a different corrective than the cool/warm frames. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 300 ml grey Acryl-sealant cartridge on a workshop table, 18% grey card in a corner. Shot under cool fluorescent light, frame tilted about 4 degrees, muted flat color. Real plastic texture, blank label surface, candid QA feel, no CGI. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool cast + ~4 deg tilt: straighten, then warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Distinct numbers from capture_01 because the light differed. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 290 ml black butyl-sealant cartridge on a bench, 18% grey card in a corner. Shot OVEREXPOSED and warm, highlights near clipping on the cartridge shoulder. Real matte-black plastic texture, blank label zone, candid documentation, no gloss. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: Overexposed AND warm: pull exposure/highlights down to recover the blown shoulder, then COOL to neutralize its grey card — opposite tonal AND WB direction from the underexposed frame 5, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Black product: protect shadow detail while neutralizing. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: capture_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~3800-4500 px long edge, of a 600 ml grey Hybrid-sealant cartridge fitted with a bright SAFETY-ORANGE nozzle cap, standing on a line-side table with a photographic 18% grey card in a corner. Shot under mixed window+fluorescent light, frame roughly level, decent exposure. Real plastic texture, blank label body, candid QA look, no CGI. The orange cap is a distinct, cleanly-separated part. Grey card visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: HERO for the colorway. Mixed light: neutralize its grey card to the shared white point (a modest correction). This graded full-res frame feeds BOTH the standard-SKU 1:1 crop AND the graphite-Pro recolor branch, so it is kept before cropping. The safety-orange cap is the recolor target — a bright, cleanly-nameable part semantic selection can isolate. Neutral filename.

inputs.name: norvexa_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Norvexa' brand wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a bold industrial sans-serif in deep charcoal, with a small chevron mark. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper rectangle and bake in the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/contrast, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. The wordmark reaches every label only as the @wordmark merge bind, so this vector is a real deliverable, not decoration.

inputs.name: ghs_pictograms_flat.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (standard regulated symbols): the three official GHS hazard pictograms this range needs — GHS02 (flame), GHS05 (corrosion) and GHS07 (exclamation mark) — supplied as THREE separate flat high-contrast PNGs, each the standard black symbol on white inside a red rotated-square (diamond) border, no gradients, clean edges, small raster size. Suitable for vectorizing so the regulated symbols stay razor-sharp at any label size.
inputs.realism_notes: Regulated CLP/GHS pictograms are supplied compliance assets (the brief's provided 'H/P statements'/hazard symbols); they are STANDARDS, not proprietary IP. Flat vector-clean raster so image_vectorize produces sharp print-safe SVGs — each of the three is vectorized once, and the roster's @pictogram column picks the correct one per SKU. Symbols are not designed, only converted.

inputs.name: ean_barcodes_perSKU.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): nine pre-rendered flat black-on-white EAN-13 barcode images, one per SKU/variant, generated by the client's barcode software at nominal press resolution — crisp high-contrast raster with clean bar edges and the human-readable digits beneath, white background. Each file named to its SKU so the roster's @barcode column can reference it.
inputs.realism_notes: Barcodes are a supplied compliance asset ('Barcodes' in the brief's provided list). They are placed at their native crisp press resolution via the @barcode merge column (downscale-only, never upscaled) — no barcode is invented, and each SKU's unique EAN is placed, not re-vectorized eight-plus times (that would be pure repetition, not depth). The vector work the brief actually rewards is on the scanned wordmark and the GHS pictograms.

outputs.name: Norvexa_labels_print_pdf_set
outputs.spec: A single print-ready CMYK PDF with 3 mm bleed at ~300 DPI carrying one page per roster row (page-count = row-count = 9) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each label binds its product_name/variant/net_content/sku/batch_prefix/h_statements/p_statements/usage_de verbatim from the roster, with its matching grey-card-neutralized product photo (via @product), its correct vectorized GHS pictogram (via @pictogram), its EAN barcode (via @barcode), and the shared vectorized wordmark in the masthead (via @wordmark) — all by merge bind, never free-form placement. The graphite-Pro colorway is one page of this set (row 9), not a separate export.

outputs.name: graded_cartridge_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened cartridge photos, delivered as the product-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point, and true-to-product (no product's genuine color forced off, the amber PU adhesive included); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered product-framed crop (the *_graded output that binds into its label) — the grey card is fully cropped OUT. The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the product crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: variant_pro_graphite.jpg
outputs.spec: Agent-authored Pro colorway of the orange-cap hero (capture_08): the bright safety-orange nozzle cap taken to a deep graphite/gunmetal finish via a masked, luminosity-preserving desaturate-and-darken on the orange band (a within-reach move — saturation driven toward zero plus a luminance drop, NOT a near-complementary hue rotation), riding the cap's existing highlights and shadow so the plastic still looks like plastic; the cartridge body and background untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill. Binds into label row 9.

outputs.name: norvexa_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the brand wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew.

outputs.name: norvexa_ghs_pictograms_svg
outputs.spec: Three vectorized GHS hazard pictograms (GHS02 flame, GHS05 corrosion, GHS07 exclamation) — each traced from its supplied flat raster into a crisp SVG that stays sharp at any label size; the roster's @pictogram column selects the correct one per SKU.

connector_workflow.note: Triage: this frame is tilted ~4 deg, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job. image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt.)

Cool fluorescent cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey; hold a neutral industrial look. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / auto_tone the killed original used).

Crop the neutralized frame to the label's product-photo frame ratio, framing on the cartridge with the grey card cropped OUT — this product crop (card removed) is what binds into the label. The pre-crop master (cap01_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop, and card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Level frame (no straighten), cool cast: warm to neutralize its grey card and match the shared white point established on frame 1; the product is white, so keep the body neutral (don't tint it warm chasing the card). Distinct numbers from frame 1. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3 deg — level it.

WARM window-light cast: this frame must move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point. Adaptive: a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. The PU wood adhesive is genuinely amber/tan and was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction from frames 1/2/6, or that 'cools' the frame because it looks amber, will neutralize the card OFF-neutral and strip the product's real color. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not by the product's appearance or the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Flat and UNDEREXPOSED: the dominant move is tonal — LIFT exposure and add contrast/clarity, THEN neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Different problem from the cool/warm frames. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~4 deg, cool cast — level it.
Cool cast: warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point; distinct numbers from the other cool frames because the light differed. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

OVEREXPOSED and warm: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown shoulder, THEN cool to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — opposite tonal AND WB direction from frame 5. Black product: hold shadow detail while neutralizing. Report the move.
Crop to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

HERO. Mixed window+fluorescent light: neutralize its grey card to the shared white point (a modest correction). Keep this full-res neutralized frame BEFORE cropping — it feeds BOTH the standard-SKU crop (step 19) AND the graphite-Pro recolor branch (steps 20-23). Report the move.
Crop the neutralized hero (orange-cap version) to the label product frame, grey card cropped OUT — binds into the standard Hybrid Pro row (row 8). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

On the graded full-res hero, semantically select ONLY the safety-orange nozzle cap ('the bright orange nozzle cap on top of the cartridge'). A real named part, not a hue or coordinate selection — isolates the recolor so the cartridge body and background stay untouched. Returns a maskURI.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes hero + cap mask): drive the ORANGE band's saturation strongly toward zero so the bright safety-orange collapses to a neutral grey, confined to the cap mask. This is a DESATURATE-and-darken (safety-orange -> graphite), a within-reach move image_adjust_hsl can hold — NOT a near-complementary hue rotation. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would grey the whole cartridge) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the cap's plastic sheen) — both are wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): drop the orange band's luminance so the now-desaturated cap settles into a deep graphite/gunmetal instead of a flat mid-grey, still riding the cap's original highlights and cast shadow so the plastic reads as plastic. A deepen-and-mute within the desaturated band, not a swing to a new hue.
Crop the finished graphite-Pro variant to the same label product frame as the set — binds into the Graphit-Edition row (row 9). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the charcoal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The wordmark is on a light ground, so its open counters read as white/transparent — a valid knockout for a light-ground mark.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. Binds to every label via the @wordmark column.

Vectorize the flat GHS02 (flame) pictogram — already flat high-contrast black-on-white in a red diamond, the ideal vectorize input, so no prep beyond the trace. Used by the flammable SKUs (rows 3, 7) via @pictogram.
Vectorize the flat GHS05 (corrosion) pictogram into crisp SVG. Used by the MS-Polymer 600 SKU (row 1) via @pictogram.
Vectorize the flat GHS07 (exclamation) pictogram into crisp SVG. Used by the irritant SKUs (rows 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9) via @pictogram.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-photo grade sub-chains fan out from the raw captures, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame: warm the cool fluorescent frames 1/2/6, cool the warm window frame 3, hold WB on the genuinely-amber PU adhesive 4, lift exposure on the underexposed Acryl 5, recover the overexposed butyl 7, modest correction on the mixed-light hero 8) followed by a crop to the label product frame, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 1/3/6 — every neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point. difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 35 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the auto_straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (cool frames warmed, one warm frame cooled, the genuinely-amber adhesive held, one underexposed frame lifted, one overexposed frame recovered) all forced to converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top are an agent-AUTHORED graphite-Pro colorway (a masked, luminosity-preserving safety-orange -> graphite desaturate-and-darken the connector can actually hold, executed as two HSL passes on a semantic cap selection, with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white wordmark scan, three vectorized regulated GHS pictograms, and a FOUR-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the master is a supplied authored .indd, the correction to the killed original which supplied a .pdf and converted it before merging); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / auto_tone stand-ins are replaced by primitive-built image_apply_adjustments; German copy and CLP H/P statements bind verbatim from the CSV; barcodes/pictograms are only placed/vectorized, not invented.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every cartridge photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master (grey card still present), reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one white point — a target the agent can miss by making the wrong per-frame call, and it must REPORT the final white-balance and exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted. The naive path — one global white balance, identical params, or a batch 'warm everything' pass across eight differently-lit frames — visibly fails to match, and the amber PU-adhesive frame is the planted trap: its card is already neutral, so any batch correction or 'cool the amber' reflex pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real product color; the correct path reads THAT card and holds WB. Card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate checked on the product crops (card cropped OUT), so neutrality is never graded on a card-removed file. Two more decision gates: mask-polarity/prep-before-trace on the wordmark (tracing the raw skewed off-white scan yields a paper-bounded fuzzy blob — the agent must straighten/crisp/crop/knock-to-transparency first), and the merge topology (a multi-record grid or a convert_pdf_to_indd template both fail to bind/produce; only the supplied single-record authored .indd with four @image columns merges, and page-count must equal row-count = 9). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit shots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction; (2) an agent-authored masked, luminosity-preserving safety-orange -> graphite cap recolor (a desaturate-and-darken within reach of image_adjust_hsl, keeping the plastic sheen, using the only masked recolor path — not color_overlay or fill_area); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed off-white wordmark scan before vectorize. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (card in frame), never on a card-removed crop; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight product crops that bind into the labels; plus the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params, the cap recolored within its mask only, the wordmark and GHS pictograms clean skew-free vectors, and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI CMYK-with-3mm-bleed label per roster row (page-count = row-count = 9).
